Onset/duration: “probably it's been about two weeks.” Marathon training and distance: “I'm currently training for a marathon… maybe like seven or eight miles… I've just done like a couple of seven mile runs.” Temporal association is implied by “I think I may have overdone my workouts and now my knees are hurting.”
No prior knee issues: “any joint problems before that?” / “not. Not really… I play some ice hockey and I had this injury a few months ago… had a huge bruise, but I think that's about it.”

Ice hockey fall and bruise: “I play some ice hockey and I had this injury a few months ago. You know, I just like fell on the ice and you know, had a huge bruise.” The specific word ‘knee’ is not stated, so attributing the bruise specifically to the knee is an addition.
Timing in run: “it probably starts like after maybe 20 minutes or so, which is probably… somewhere around mile three, maybe and a half or three miles.”

Worse with flexion/extension doing abs: “when I do my abs, it kind of requires me to… go from the flex position of my knees and straighten my legs. Then I hear all this clicking.” She also notes pain getting worse around that time.

Tingling description: “there was this tingling in my toes. Like, after the run, there was tingling in my toes, like, on my, you know, my right toes… it was just that time… no [current altered sensation].” No color/temperature change: “Any change in color or temperature of your lower legs?” / “Nope.”

Sock indentation and swelling: “if you stand for a long time, your feet will kind of… swell up… I notice it because of my socks… this indentation… it's not like, major.” No calf pain/pitting: “any pain in the back of the calf…?” / “No, nothing like that? No.” She is unsure about pitting: “I don't know if I really try that… Do you mean I just need to like, press and see what happens?” so ‘without persistent edema’ reasonably summarizes absence of described persistent swelling.

Initial swelling only: “Does the knee look swollen?” / “Well, it did. Like, the first time I ran, it was a little bit swollen… but… it went away. But right now, right now it's not swollen.” ‘Now intermittent’ is slightly stronger, but she clearly describes initial swelling that resolved and none currently.

Full ROM: “are you able to fully straighten the leg?” / “Yes.” and “what about fully flex it?” / “Yes.”

Urgent review advice: “if… you develop like persistent swelling, heat, redness of the knee or high temperature, feel unwell, or it completely locks up and you can't bend and stretch it, then you'd need to see a doctor urgently. So call us back in that case.”

Imaging after physio/if needed: “physiotherapist… can do like a long assessment… and then make an assessment as to whether we need to do any imagery to have a look inside the knee.” This implies imaging considered after physio evaluation if concern persists.
This restates the urgent review advice: “if… persistent swelling, heat, redness of the knee or high temperature, feel unwell, or it completely locks up… then you'd need to see a doctor urgently.”

Follow-up imaging: “physiotherapist… then make an assessment as to whether we need to do any imagery to have a look inside the knee.” This is imaging consideration after physio review if still indicated.

Back pain is explicitly queried and not affirmed: “any back pain…?” with no back pain reported in the response.

Systemic symptoms (fever, feeling unwell) are only mentioned as warning signs to seek urgent care and are never reported as present; stomach/asthma/indigestion are denied: “No problems.” This supports absence of systemic symptoms.
